decisions.reason: Although recent standalone visibility is low, the product directly extends the firm's core second-channel authentication capabilities, so its knowledge base and R&D make retention and integration more likely than withdrawal.
This architecture sits at the center of the firm's cryptography and platform expertise, and high absorptive capacity favors continued development or bundling rather than exit.
As a narrower delivery use case with weaker standalone visibility, it is easier to absorb its functionality into broader secure-communication offerings and reallocate resources.
The hardware token is related to the firm's skills but less central than its software-led identity strategy, so limited prominence and likely adoption constraints make withdrawal likely.
Compliance-oriented payment security still fits the firm's regulated authentication and transaction knowledge, so it is more likely to be retained, even if repositioned within the broader platform.
